sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about Roman ships: Romans learned shipbuilding from Greeks and Egyptians (not the other way). Mortise and tenon method required skilled craftsmen. Later Mediterranean practice: frame first, then hull (not hull before frame). Romans called the Mediterranean 'Mare Nostrum' because they dominated it — TRUE. Most rowers were slaves, not soldiers/army. Warships: lightweight, fast, stayed afloat, sailed close to land, bronze battering ram for attacking enemy timber and oars, trireme had rowers on three levels/decks. Merchant ships: broad keel deep below sea surface, steered with rudders and tiller bar, had square and lateen sails, used music/drumming to synchronise rowers. Transported grain to Ostia and Puteoli (ports in Italy), pulled ashore by oxen/animals, navigated by landmarks.]
